result.journal: Proc. ACM Meas. Anal. Comput. Syst.
result.keywords: Cloud resource provisioning and load balancing both face volatile demand, where dispatching and scheduling decisions must be made online under uncertainty. This paper studies prediction-aware dispatching policies for cloud systems with server-side SRPT scheduling, focusing on how imperfect forecasts affect response time and regret. We propose a lightweight guardrail mechanism that can wrap around standard dispatchers, and we analyze its performance under heavy traffic using a regret-style framework. Empirical experiments on synthetic and trace-driven workloads show that prediction errors vary by workload class and time horizon, while theoretical bounds demonstrate that the augmented policy remains robust and near-optimal in congested regimes.
result.title: Adaptive Guardrails for Cloud Scheduling: Prediction-Aware Dispatching Under Heavy Traffic
